facts.text: The study compared equiatomic Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 films with Re-containing equiatomic Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 films before and after He irradiation.
The films were implanted with 120 keV He2+ at a fluence of 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2 and a dose rate of 1 × 10^13 ions/cm^2/s for 1000 s.
He implantation and subsequent mechanical testing were performed at room temperature.
Nanoindentation was performed in continuous-stiffness mode to a maximum depth of 200 nm at a strain rate of 0.05 s^-1, using 10 indents per sample.
Approximately 1.7 μm-diameter micropillars with a 2:1 height-to-diameter ratio were compressed in situ at 1 nm/s.
Re addition produced several-nanometer-wide amorphous regions at grain boundaries and increased the density of defect-sink sites.

The grain boundaries, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous boundary regions in NbMoTaWRe promoted annihilation of irradiation-induced vacancies and suppressed He-bubble growth and segregation.
After irradiation, NbMoTaW contained larger He bubbles aligned and segregated along grain boundaries, whereas obvious bubbles and boundary segregation were not discernible in NbMoTaWRe.
Relative to irradiated NbMoTaW, irradiated NbMoTaWRe exhibited substantially less irradiation-induced hardening and grain-boundary embrittlement.
Irradiation reduced the micropillar compressive strength of NbMoTaW but increased the compressive strength of NbMoTaWRe.
NbMoTaWRe showed no obvious nanoindentation hardening after He implantation, while NbMoTaW required a slightly higher indentation load at the same displacement.
For NbMoTaWRe, the compressive strain before a marked stress drop changed from approximately 0.065 before irradiation to approximately 0.055 after irradiation.
